// diagnostic

E0748

`-[via {param}]>` on `{fn}` names no such parameter or a parameter that isn't a callback.

What

`-[via {param}]>` on `{fn}` names no such parameter or a parameter that isn't a callback.

Why

`-[via f]>` publishes a function's effects as a tight pass-through of its callback parameter `f` (D-EFF2); `f` must be a parameter of the function whose type is a `fn(…)`.

Fix

Point `via` at a function-typed parameter, or drop the `-[via …]>` annotation.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0748: tests/ui/effect_via_unknown_param.stderr.

Error [E0112]: `invoke` wants fn(Int) -[IO]> for argument 2, but this is fn(n: Int) !Err
  --> tests/ui/effect_via_unknown_param.jet:7:22
    |
  7 | fn run() { invoke(5, show) }
    |                      ^^^^
 Why: every argument must match its parameter's type
 Fix: use fn(Int) -[IO]> here

Error [E0748]: `-[via missing]>` on `invoke` names no such parameter
  --> tests/ui/effect_via_unknown_param.jet:3:46
    |
  3 | fn invoke(n: Int, act: fn(Int) -[IO]>) -[via missing]> { act(n) }
    |                                              ^^^^^^^
 Why: `-[via f]>` publishes the effects of a callback parameter `f`; `invoke` has no parameter called `missing`
 Fix: name one of `invoke`'s callback parameters after `via`
